items.title: Add MultiRect command

milestone.title: 4.x
milestone.description: Issues and pull requests slated for an undetermined Godot 4 release.

items.body:
Superseding: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/70415
Porting: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/68960 for Godot ~4.7

This is a port of the Multirect batching command for Godot 4.7. This is largely derived from @lawnjelly's implementation of this feature in both Godot 3.x and the draft he published in PR #70415 - I rebased the Draft onto 4.7 and finished implementing the MultiRect Command in both the Forward+ Renderer and the Compatibility renderer.

Repetitive Rect Drawing Commands (such as rendering large amounts of text) can still be taxing on the CPU as the Command Batcher re-processes some redundant information for every single Rect. Using a Multirect command can indicate to the Batcher that it should skip much of the redundant processing! 

### This implements:
* The Backend for MultiRect commands in both Forward+ and compatibility
* A Helper Class for preparing MultiRects, called RendererCanvasHelper, common to the whole Rendering Server
* Basic usage of MultiRects by Label Nodes.
* Basic usage of MultiRects by TileMapLayer Nodes.

### Basic Performance Measurements
Performing a brief test (on my particular computer) by having a label render 355,200 characters:
* Stable 4.6 -- Compatibility Renderer -- averages 11.3 CPU milliseconds per Frame
* MultiRect 4.7 -- Compatibility Render -- averages 3.6 CPU milliseconds per Frame
* Stable 4.6 -- Forward + Renderer -- averages 4.3 CPU milliseconds per Frame
* MultiRect 4.7 -- Forward+ Renderer --  averages 2.2 CPU milliseconds per Frame

TileMap test, render about 1.8 million Tiles on my computer.
* Stable 4.6 -- Compatibility -- Average 28 CPU milliseconds per frame
* Multirect 4.7 -- Compatibility -- Average 10 CPU milliseconds per frame
* Stable 4.6 -- Forward+ -- Average 10 CPU milliseconds per frame
* Multirect 4.7 -- Forward+ -- Average 5 CPU milliseconds per frame.


Using this project to test the performance (Taken & Modified from LawnJelly's original PR). 
[batch_test_text.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25699424/batch_test_text.zip)

Control.tscn has a Label with buttons to add 44k Characters of text to the label.
Tiles.tscn has a Tilemap that is roughly 1.2k x 1.2k tiles being rendered at 0.1 Scale (So all ~1.8 million tiles are attempted to render rather than being culled for being off screen).
Using the in-editor profiler for measurements.

items.title: Preserve visual layer of meshes in GridMap nodes

milestone.title: 4.x
milestone.description: Issues and pull requests slated for an undetermined Godot 4 release.

items.body:
### Description
This PR adds visual layer property to `MeshLibrary` items allowing to preserve `MeshInstance` nodes visual layer when used in `GridMap` nodes.

That is long missing feature for `GridMap` node requested even since Godot 3 (see #40245) and possibility for setting different render layers may be required to achieve some rendering effects.

This change should work also for `GridMap`s using baked meshes.

#### Note 1:
To use this new feature you need to recreate your `MeshLibrary` resource (export your tileset source scene as `MeshLibrary` again) or update your old `MeshLibrary` items visual layer by hand.

#### Note 2:
If you are already using baked meshes in your project to use new feature you need to invalidate old baked meshes (for example by modifying `GridMap` cells) and re-bake.

### Example
As an example usage now it is possible to use `Decal` cull property to draw some "selection area" only on floors and avoid texture being mapped also on walls (impossible before when using `GridMap` for floors & walls).

![GridmapRenderLayers](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cd2eb0d8-a0a0-44bd-b97f-14b50f869ff8)

items.title: Resources loaded through GDScript `preload()` are never unloaded
items.body: ### Tested versions Tested on v4.0.4 and v4.6.2 stable builds. Behavior is likely the same in all other 4.x versions. ### System information Godot v4.6.2.stable (71f334935) - Freedesktop SDK 25.08 (Flatpak runtime) on Wayland - Wayland display driver, Multi-window, 1 monitor - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - AMD Radeon 760M Graphics (radeonsi, phoenix, LLVM 21.1.8, DRM 3.64, 6.18.13-200.fc43.x86_64) - AMD Ryzen 5 7640U w/ Radeon 760M Graphics (12 threads) - 14.92 GiB memory ### Issue description I'm not actually sure if this is actually a bug, or just undocumented behavior, so there could be room for discussion. At least through a quick search in the docs, I can't find any warning that `preload()` is unable to unload resources, and yet, [it is widely recommended as the default option in official docs pages](https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Agodotengine%2Fgodot-docs%20preload&type=code), and many non-official tutorials as well. Why this is a problem: due to its recommended status, many developers have the impression that `preload()` is faster and more performant than other resource loading methods, which it could be in small games that can fit entirely in RAM + VRAM, but as projects scale up and more resources are added to them, so does increase the likelihood of more resources being preloaded. This causes them to be pinned to memory for the entirety of the game's runtime, with no clear warning signs of how bad this can be. As a consequence, if a game preloads heavy scenes, such as entire levels, a long session might cause the game to slow down or even crash, due to the continuous pile-up of resources that never get cleaned up by Godot. That means using `preload()` is as dangerous as creating cyclic references between RefCounted objects, if not more because resources can contain large amounts of data. Notes: - This is not a memory leak, because the resources can still be loaded from the cache, so a specific resource won't be instantiated multiple times. - This seems to be directly caused by #77513, since preloads are held by compiled scripts. - Despite the similar name, the ResourcePreloader node is not affected by this. Its resources are held by the scene resource, same as `@export` vars. Example included in MRP. ### Steps to reproduce - Create some kind of resource or scene with a script; - Load another resource in that script, using the `preload()` macro; - Create an instance of the script, and then free the instance (and if using a scene, release references to it); - Use any method to verify that the preloaded resource is still in memory (ie. WeakRef.get_ref(), or static memory monitor). MRP contains a WeakRef-based example. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) Project structure: - main.tscn - startup scene - icon.tscn - scene loaded dynamically by main.tscn, with its own dependencies - resources/* - plain Resource instances that are used by icon.tscn Use "Spawn Icon" button to add an instance of the icon and print some logs, then "Delete Icon" to delete the latest added icon instance and print more logs about its resources. Notice "script_preloaded" never becomes null through the WeakRef. Expected: - when the last icon instance is deleted, all unused resources should be freed OR - docs are updated to reflect `preload()` sticky memory behavior Logs: MRP Link: [preload-no-unload.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26681189/preload-no-unload.zip)

items.title: Duplicating child node of scene instance or inherited scene copies signal binding locked state (yellow), preventing disconnecting until editor restart
items.body: ### Tested versions - Reproducible in: v4.6.stable.official [89cea1439] ### System information Godot v4.6.stable - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3070 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.6636) - 12th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-12900K (24 threads) - 63.75 GiB memory ### Issue description In those two cases: 1. Creating an inherited scene from a base scene with signals on children and duplicating a child with signals 2. Instantiating a scene in another scene, enabling Editable Children and duplicating a child with signals The resulting child will have the pre-existing signals marked in yellow (not editable), preventing disconnection. This is only a transient bug: restarting the editor will clear the yellow mark and allow edition/disconnection. ### Steps to reproduce ## Setting up the project (already done in MRP, only need to do this once) 1. Create menu.tscn with Menu > Button 2. Add menu.gd script to Menu 3. Connect Button's pressed signal to menu.gd > `_on_button_pressed` method ### Scene instance 1. Create demo.tscn and add instance of menu.tscn 2. Enable Editable Children on that instance ### Inherited scene 1. Create New Inherited Scene from menu.tscn, named menu_inherited.tscn ## Bug repro (you must repeat these steps after every editor restart) ### Scene instance 1. In demo.tscn, duplicate the Button node 2. Check the Signals panel Actual: non-editable, non-disconnectable (yellow) signal binding to `_on_button_pressed` Expected: editable (white) signal binding to `_on_button_pressed` 3. Restart the editor The signal is now editable. ### Inherited scene 1. Open menu_inherited.tscn and duplicate the Button node 2. Check the Signals panel Actual: non-editable, non-disconnectable (yellow) signal binding to `_on_button_pressed` Expected: editable (white) signal binding to `_on_button_pressed` 3. Restart the editor The signal is now editable. ## Notes When copy-pasting a node instead of duplicating it, the signals are not copied at all, so the bug is not visible (not sure if intended or not, I suppose copy-pasting could be done to another location where the signal callback is not reachable and that's the reason why signal bindings are not copied) ## Workaround Same, copy the node and paste it into its parent for a duplicate without the signals at all (you'll have to manually re-add signals you need though) ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [mrp-duplicate-inherited-or-instantiated-scene-child-cannot-disconnect-signal.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25995960/mrp-duplicate-inherited-or-instantiated-scene-child-cannot-disconnect-signal.zip)

items.title: Slider with negative min_value initializes to the wrong value
items.body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: 4.7-beta1. Also reproducible in 4.0 (this did not regress any time recently).

### System information

Godot v4.7.beta1 - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4080 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.9636) - AMD Ryzen 7 5700X 8-Core Processor (16 threads) - 15.92 GiB memory - WASAPI (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

When a slider has a negative `min_value` (for some reason this only repros with small negative values like 0.2), and a `value` of 0.0, it behaves correctly in the editor, but when the project is run, the slider initializes to the wrong default value. Instead of being set to 0.0, it can initialize all the way left, or right, or somewhere else in between, depending on the minimum value.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a slider.
2. Set its min_value to a small negative (e.g. -0.2). For some reason, this doesn't work for larger values like -1.0.
3. Leave or explicitly set its value to 0.0.
4. Optionally: log or display the value of the slider.
5. Run the project.

Expected behaviour: the slider's initial value is 0.0 (i.e. not all the way to the left, because of the negative minimum).
Observed behaviour: the slider's initial value is -0.2 (all the way to the left).

Bizarrely, for some minimum values (e.g. -0.5) the slider starts all the way to the right instead.

Notice: In the .tscn file, the "value" is not stored at all, because it is the default of 0.0. I'm not sure if this is a clue (the slider might assume incorrectly that the default value is not 0.0 but in fact all the way left).

items.body:
### Godot version

4.0dev

### Issue description

From version to version, some resources changed format. While we have `ClassDB::add_compatibility_class` to help with class renames, we kind of have to keep a lot of old properties in resources to keep compatibility with previous versions.

While most of those properties are surrounded by `#ifndef DISABLE_DEPRECATED`, those end up cluttering the API (as most of them can be accessed via the `set()` function). Also, like in the TileSet case, we have no way to operate a conversion depending on several old properties at once, as there is no callback called on the object once a resource is imported.

Consequently, we discussed with @reduz that it would be better to handle conversion from version to version using a dedicated system. That would probably require saving a version number inside the project (or each resource maybe, to support plugins ?) to check if a resource needs an update. The conversion would likely be called after a resource is imported I guess.

Here is a tracker for resources having compatibility properties that could be moved to such a system (some might be missing):
- [ ] TileMap ("tile_data")
- [ ] TileSet
- [ ] AnimationPlayer ("playback/play")
- [ ] CanvasItem ("show_on_top")
- [ ] BoxShape3D ("entends")
- [ ] Environment ("background_sky", "background_sky_custom_fov", "background_sky_orientation")
- [ ] Font ("font_data", "fallback/")
- [ ] ShaderMaterial ("param/", "shader_param")
- [ ] Mesh ("surfaces/*")
- [ ] MultiMesh ("transform_array", "transform_2d_array", "color_array", "custom_data_array")
- [ ] RectangleShape2D ("extents")
- [ ] SpriteFrames ("frames")

items.title: The value format of `_spawnable_scenes` property of `MultiplayerSpawner` in .tscn is different between 4.4.dev3 and 4.4.dev6
items.body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in 4.4.dev6 official and 4.4.dev3 official

### System information

Godot v4.4.dev3 - Windows 10.0.22631 - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 Ti (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.6094) - 13th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-13600KF (20 threads)

### Issue description

When use 4.4.dev3 and set the property in Node `MultiplayerSpawner`'s `Auto Spawn List`, the saved value in .tscn is like:
```
[node name="Slot1Spawner" type="MultiplayerSpawner" parent="."]
_spawnable_scenes = PackedStringArray("res://player_head.tscn")
```

When use 4.4.dev6 and do the same, the saved value in .tscn is like:
```
[node name="Slot1Spawner" type="MultiplayerSpawner" parent="."]
_spawnable_scenes = PackedStringArray("uid://docb3aisq4txw")
```

Is this supposed to happen? A bug or not? I think using PackedStringArray("res://player_head.tscn") is better than using PackedStringArray("uid://docb3aisq4txw") but I'm not so sure. 

Can an older version Godot understand `_spawnable_scenes = PackedStringArray("uid://docb3aisq4txw")` ? This behavior might **breaks compatibility** which is not mentioned before.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bb5000ef-de38-4fb3-a730-158d42e69748)


### Steps to reproduce

1. using 4.4.dev3, create a project
2. create a scene
3. add a `MultiplayerSpawner` node
4. edit it's property `Auto Spawn List` then add an element, then choose another scene.
5. save and see the value saved in .tscn file
6. Do the same in 4.4.dev6 and compare .tscn file.

NA

items.title: `AnimationPlayer` changes `.tscn` file on save and creates noise in version control if connected to enabled `AnimationTree`
items.body:
### Tested versions

Godot Engine v4.2.1.stable.mono.official.b09f793f5

### System information

Godot v4.2.1.stable.mono - Windows 10.0.22631 - GLES3 (Compatibility) - NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3070 Laptop GPU (NVIDIA; 31.0.15.4630) - AMD Ryzen 7 5800H with Radeon Graphics (16 Threads)

### Issue description

I have an `AnimationPlayer` that change the `frame` property of my `AnimatedSprite2D`s `Animation` component. This `AnimationPlayer` is connected to an ``AnimationTree`.

If the `AnimationTree` is active in the editor, the `frame` property is change on disk when saving the scene that contains the animated node, and every time I try to commit something in `git`, I see an update to the `tscn` file. Even if I didn't touch the scene as part of my workflow, the property is still modified on save. You can see the values updating live in the editor as well while the tree is running.

For example:

before
```
[node name="Sprite2D" type="Sprite2D" parent="."]
texture = ExtResource("1_5rya8")
hframes = 4
frame = 1
```

after
```
[node name="Sprite2D" type="Sprite2D" parent="."]
texture = ExtResource("1_5rya8")
hframes = 4
frame = 4
```

### Steps to reproduce

Animate a property of some scene via an `AnimationPlayer`.
Connect it to an `AnimationTree`.
Enable the `AnimationTree`.
Save the scene without modifying the `frame` property
Observe that sometimes the scene's `tscn` is modified with a new value for property.



### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[mrp.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/15751605/mrp.zip)
